Use case: identity-preserve
Asset type: one isolated source image for a single 96x96 runtime character frame in a 2D pixel-art RPG
Input images: Image 1 is the accepted Ruins Bell Prowler neutral profile and locks the exact identity, proportions, palette, and materials. Image 2 is the accepted attack-2-v2 and confirms the same character's construction and pixel-art finish; use its pose only where this frame description explicitly calls for it.
Subject: The same low, heavy four-legged stone beast facing RIGHT, with overlapping slate-gray stone plates, restrained olive moss seams, broad short legs and feet, a blunt lowered head, a cracked chipped weathered copper bell shell strapped across its back, and one short chain with a single small dark clapper. Preserve the exact accepted character identity and compact scale.
Style/medium: crisp 2D pixel-art RPG sprite; stepped pixel edges, clean readable pixel clusters, chunky dark outlines, limited muted palette, sharp contrast and hard edges, consistent with both references; no painterly rendering, no 3D.
Composition/framing: a single complete side-view beast, head toward the RIGHT, centered on a square transparent canvas, bottom-centered pivot, all four legs, tail, full bell and clapper inside the canvas, generous transparent padding, same visual size as the profile reference. One frozen pose only, never a sheet.
Constraints: genuinely transparent background; preserve the same body and bell construction; clear limb silhouette at small game size; no crop; body stays fully opaque and intact.
Avoid: other creatures, duplicate limbs, separate parts, motion streaks, fake projectile, impact flash, magic, glow, cast shadow, ground plane, background, scenery, text, lettering, symbols, watermark, grid, blur, gradients, blood, left-facing view.
Primary request: Create the attack-0 anticipation pose, the opening instant before the low sweep windup. Keep all four paws grounded. The beast lowers its blunt head and compresses its shoulders slightly while its weight begins shifting back into the hindquarters; the near-side front shoulder draws back only a little, with that paw still planted beneath the chest. The pose must read as a quiet, readable preparation, not the actual sweep and not a copy of idle. The bell remains strapped in place; its clapper hangs naturally.
